newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NFI FORTUNA UNDAMAGED BY FLOODS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NFI FORTUNA UNDAMAGED BY FLOODS.

text.p: Firms under Poland's National Investment Fund Fortuna SA (NFI XIII) were not badly hit by floods in the south and its construction companies may benefit from rebuilding business, its investment director said.
"None of our firms suffered losses except for companies in Silesia which had to spend some small amounts on flood security preparations," Jerzy Kowalczyk said on Thursday.
Kowalczyk said that while another flood wave was expected this weekend, firms grouped under Fortuna would be safe.
He told Reuters that Fortuna's outlook looked positive as construction firms made up a large part of its portfolio second only to artificial fibre producers.
"People have suffered terribly, but we must admit that construction companies will benefit (from the flood) as demand for their services increases," said Kowalczyk.
Fortuna describes itself as a restructuring-growth fund and plans to evolve into a typical investment fund. It plans to float five companies in 1997 and 1998.
Under the Polish government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms. Each NFI has 31,026,185 shares.
